name: Infrastructure and homologation

initiation_authorization.evidence: Human explicitly authorized implementation of Phase 09 on 2026-08-14 after approving the Coolify topology with PostgreSQL separate and the remaining runtime in one application stack.

expected_features: Coolify-ready homologation stack with web, worker-default, worker-integrations, Beat and Redis sharing the approved application image.
PostgreSQL 17 remains a separate exclusive Coolify database resource addressed only through DATABASE_URL.
Explicit release/migration job that runs independently from the long-lived web and Celery processes.
Production-grade homologation settings, healthchecks, fail-closed external effects and secret-only runtime configuration.
Operational runbook for empty-database bootstrap, migrations, health validation, backup/restore evidence, rollback and observability readiness.
CI validation of the homologation Compose topology without requiring real credentials or external provider access.
deferred_features: real provider activation unless separately authorized by an explicit homologation subgate
public provider callbacks unless separately authorized

states.rule: Phase 09 adds no canonical business lifecycle; it prepares and validates infrastructure and homologation only.

snapshots: No persistent domain snapshot is introduced by infrastructure work.
Logs, metrics and backup evidence must not contain secrets or unrestricted personal data.
idempotency: Release migrations must be safe to run repeatedly at the same approved application version.
Bootstrap and operational scripts must fail safely when prerequisites are missing and must not duplicate privileged seed state.
Provider-specific idempotency remains governed by the owning domain and is not relaxed by homologation.
money_rules: Infrastructure never computes or mutates canonical money.
Payment provider activation remains blocked unless an explicit provider homologation subgate is authorized.
authorization: All application authorization and Organization isolation rules from approved phases remain unchanged.
Runtime configuration must not introduce hostname tenancy, shared Flowlog identity, shared database access or arbitrary Organization selection.
Background workers continue to revalidate Organization and entity boundaries through approved services/selectors.

required: homologation Compose config renders with PostgreSQL external to the application stack
web, worker-default, worker-integrations, Beat and Redis topology
release migration command is explicit and non-long-lived
production/homologation settings fail closed without provider enablement
backup/restore and rollback procedures are documented and independently verifiable before final approval
tests.sandbox_contract_validation: Deferred until a provider-specific homologation subgate receives separate explicit authorization.

coverage.domain_expectation: No reduction in approved domain coverage; any new executable infrastructure helper requires direct tests where applicable.

ci: migration consistency and historical rollback gates
documentation: runtime environment variables and secret handling
acceptance_criteria: Phase 09 is based on actual_base_sha 12b519c3e8237e1ebe43c1a0253b0747e0680e07 and approved Phase 08 product head 8ec559ab69b88fbd781144b1ad9dc00d465193c2.
Homologation application stack contains web, worker-default, worker-integrations, Beat and Redis, while PostgreSQL 17 is external to that stack and exclusive to Vidalys Flow.
No database, Redis, runtime, secrets, infrastructure or identity is reused from Flowlog.
Migrations run through an explicit release job against an empty PostgreSQL 17 database contract.
Only the web service is intended for ingress; Redis and Celery services have no public ports.
External effects remain fail-closed by default and no provider/sandbox/callback is activated without a separate explicit authorization.
Backup/restore, rollback, observability and health validation procedures are documented before the phase can become a review candidate.
Total coverage remains at least 85% and Foundation CI is green on the material candidate.
Independent Review and QA/Security GO are required before final human approval.
Production go-live, cutover, release and Phase 10 require separate explicit human authorization.
checks: docker compose config for local, test and homologation definitions

handoff_format.base_sha_semantics: Exact origin/main SHA resolved before branch creation.

allowed_scope: Coolify-oriented homologation application stack and runtime configuration for approved Vidalys Flow code.
External PostgreSQL resource contract with internal/private connectivity only.
Redis within the application stack for Celery broker and cache.
Explicit release job, healthchecks, observability hooks, backup/restore and rollback runbooks.
Offline/CI homologation validation with no real secrets or external provider effects.
forbidden_scope: Production go-live, cutover or Flowlog shutdown.
Real provider, sandbox, credential, public callback or DNS change without a separately authorized homologation subgate.
New business lifecycle or domain semantics.
Phase 10 implementation or release without separate explicit human authorization.
